intro: An Alabama artist and improviser, new to records late in life.
story: Lonnie Holley, born in Birmingham in 1950 and based in Atlanta, was a celebrated sculptor of found objects before he began recording in his early sixties, and his first album, Just Before Music, came out in 2012. He played Pickathon in 2014 and again in 2018, the year MITH, recorded over five years with Richard Swift, Sam Gendel and others, came out on Jagjaguwar and landed on twelve year-end lists. The New Yorker's Amanda Petrusich wrote about it that October. He was named a USA Artist Fellow in 2022, Oh Me Oh My followed in March 2023, and Tonky in 2025.
artist_reel_line: Tonky came out on Jagjaguwar in 2025.

story: Sierra Hull signed to Rounder at 13 and had won the IBMA's Mandolin Player of the Year in 2016 and 2017 when she played Pickathon in 2018. Weighted Mind, produced by Béla Fleck and built mostly on mandolin and bass, came out on Rounder in January 2016 and was nominated for a Grammy for Best Folk Album; NPR heard an altogether different singer-songwriter emerge. 25 Trips came in 2020, and both records reached No. 1 on Billboard's Bluegrass chart. She has toured with Fleck since 2021, and A Tip Toe High Wire was nominated for the 2026 Grammy for Best Bluegrass Album.
artist_reel_line: A Tip Toe High Wire was nominated for Best Bluegrass Album in 2026.

intro: A Tuareg desert-blues collective from Mali.
story: Tinariwen is the Tuareg guitar collective from the southern Sahara, between northeastern Mali and southern Algeria, whose Tassili won the 2012 Grammy for Best World Music Album. Elwan, their seventh album, came out in February 2017 with Andrew Scheps engineering, and was nominated for the same Grammy in January 2018. They played Pickathon that summer, their second visit after 2015, and NPR's First Listen heard sweetness and hope on the record. Amadjar was nominated for Best Global Music Album in 2021, and Hoggar came out on Wedge in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Hoggar came out on Wedge in 2026.
